sn55.26:3.1: “Sir, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika is sick, suffering, gravely ill.
sn55.26:3.2: He bows with his head to your feet.
sn55.26:3.4: ‘Sir, please visit him at his home out of sympathy.’”
sn55.26:10.3: Seeing in yourself that right purpose, that pain may die down on the spot.
sn55.26:11.3: Seeing in yourself that right speech, that pain may die down on the spot.
sn55.26:12.3: Seeing in yourself that right action, that pain may die down on the spot.
sn55.26:13.3: Seeing in yourself that right livelihood, that pain may die down on the spot.
sn55.26:14.3: Seeing in yourself that right effort, that pain may die down on the spot.
sn55.26:15.3: Seeing in yourself that right mindfulness, that pain may die down on the spot.
sn55.26:16.3: Seeing in yourself that right immersion, that pain may die down on the spot.
sn55.26:17.3: Seeing in yourself that right knowledge, that pain may die down on the spot.
